title: D. Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap

legend: You are given n$$$n$$$ pairs of integers (a1,b1),(a2,b2),…,(an,bn)$$$(a_1, b_1), (a_2, b_2), \ldots, (a_n, b_n)$$$. All of the integers in the pairs are distinct and are in the range from 1$$$1$$$ to 2⋅n$$$2 \cdot n$$$ inclusive.
Let's call a sequence of integers x1,x2,…,x2k$$$x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{2k}$$$ good if either
x1<x2>x3<…<x2k−2>x2k−1<x2k$$$x_1  \lt  x_2  \gt  x_3  \lt  \ldots  \lt  x_{2k-2}  \gt  x_{2k-1}  \lt  x_{2k}$$$, or

You need to choose a subset of distinct indices i1,i2,…,it$$$i_1, i_2, \ldots, i_t$$$ and their order in a way that if you write down all numbers from the pairs in a single sequence (the sequence would be ai1,bi1,ai2,bi2,…,ait,bit$$$a_{i_1}, b_{i_1}, a_{i_2}, b_{i_2}, \ldots, a_{i_t}, b_{i_t}$$$), this sequence is good.
What is the largest subset of indices you can choose? You also need to construct the corresponding index sequence i1,i2,…,it$$$i_1, i_2, \ldots, i_t$$$.
input: The first line contains single integer n$$$n$$$ (2≤n≤3⋅105$$$2 \leq n \leq 3 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of pairs.
Each of the next n$$$n$$$ lines contain two numbers — ai$$$a_i$$$ and bi$$$b_i$$$ (1≤ai,bi≤2⋅n$$$1 \le a_i, b_i \le 2 \cdot n$$$) — the elements of the pairs.
It is guaranteed that all integers in the pairs are distinct, that is, every integer from 1$$$1$$$ to 2⋅n$$$2 \cdot n$$$ is mentioned exactly once.
output: In the first line print a single integer t$$$t$$$ — the number of pairs in the answer.
Then print t$$$t$$$ distinct integers i1,i2,…,it$$$i_1, i_2, \ldots, i_t$$$ — the indexes of pairs in the corresponding order.
note: The final sequence in the first example is 1<7>3<5>2<10$$$1  \lt  7  \gt  3  \lt  5  \gt  2  \lt  10$$$.
The final sequence in the second example is 6>1<3>2<5>4$$$6  \gt  1  \lt  3  \gt  2  \lt  5  \gt  4$$$.
